newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand sees slow finance sector recovery.
newsitem.headline: Thailand sees slow finance sector recovery.

text.p: Thailand said on Friday that it expected its ailing finance sector to make a slow recovery through the rest of this year, adding that stronger companies will emerge after recent tough steps taken by the government to consolidate the sector.

"For the rest of the year we will see slow recovery in the finance sector. We will have a lesser number but stronger finance companies in the next two to three months," Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee told reporters.

The government recently suspended 16 weak finance firms and forced them to merge with five core, stronger firms. They have been given until July 11 to come up with some plans or face closure or forced mergers. The finance sector is riddled with overexposure to cash-strapped and depressed property firms.

The minister also said that Thailand would revise its 10 percent target for exports growth this year after Wednesday's flotation of the baht which was in effect a de facto devaluation of between 15-20 percent. His ministry would hold meetings with exporters to come up with a fresh target for 1997. Thai exports have been sluggish recently and in 1996 growth contracted 0.2 percent from growth of mroe than 23 percent in 1995. Analysts expect the baht's drop after the flotation will help boost Thai exports significantly.

Narongchai also said that the government would monitor consumer prices closely to prevent profiteering by unscrupulous businesses and keep inflation under control after the baht float which could initially cause irrational behaviour.
